problem:
Consider the line $y=2x-3$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=12.$
worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=2x-3$ passes through the points $A(0,-3)$ and $B(1,-1)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $A$ and $B$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -6 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${A}^{′}(0,-6)$ and ${B}^{′}(2,-1).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y+6 & =\frac{-1+6}{2-0}(x-0) \\ y+6 & =\frac{5}{2}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y+6 & =\frac{5}{2}x \\ 2y+12 & =5x \\ 5x-2y & =12\end{aligned}
$$
